title: Summary Cloze: A New Task for Content Selection in Topic-Focused Summarization
research_question: Can next-sentence prediction conditioned on a topic, reference documents, and the summary-so-far provide a scalable task for learning content selection in topic-focused summarization?
methodology: The authors define the summary cloze task, where a model must generate the next summary sentence given a topic, reference material, and a partial summary, and construct the WIKICITE dataset from cited sentences in Wikipedia articles about living people. They collect 486,015 instances and evaluate extractive baselines plus a two-stage system that first selects reference sentences and then generates a cloze with a pointer-generator model conditioned on the preceding summary context. Evaluation uses ROUGE, perplexity, ablations of topic and context, oracle comparisons, and a small human study in which manually written clozes are judged for continuation quality.

key_findings.finding: Access to the topic and preceding summary context helped human writers select content closer to the reference cloze, with human ROUGE-1 increasing from 24.49 without topic/context to 31.78 with them.
The learned extractive ContentSelector outperformed the non-oracle extractive baselines, reaching ROUGE-1 25.13 versus 21.33 for BM25 and 17.50 for Lead-1.
Most of the ContentSelector improvement from conditioning came from the partial-summary context; removing the topic alone did not produce a statistically significant degradation.

Conditioning the abstractive decoder on the preceding summary context improved generated clozes across tested preprocessing variants, including roughly a two-point ROUGE-1 gain with ContentSelector preprocessing.
The model design uses coverage together with the preceding summary context to discourage generation of information already expressed in that context, directly addressing local repetition.
A large gap remained between learned extraction and oracle extraction, indicating substantial unresolved content-selection headroom.
ROUGE is an imperfect measure for this task because many different next sentences can be valid; the paper reports only moderate correlation between ROUGE and crowd quality judgments.

limitations: The task isolates sentence-level content selection rather than evaluating a complete evolving summarization system.
WIKICITE is derived from Wikipedia articles in the Living people category and therefore differs substantially from workplace communication.
The construction assumes that a cited reference document contains the information expressed in the associated Wikipedia sentence, despite noisy web extraction and citation practices.
Only one observed cloze serves as the automatic reference even though multiple next sentences can be valid.
ROUGE has difficulty distinguishing alternative valid continuations and showed only moderate correlation with human quality judgments.

The experiments model preceding textual context but do not represent explicit temporal state transitions, supersession, open-versus-resolved status, user-specific priorities, or longitudinal briefing delivery.
raw_claims: The summary cloze task predicts the next summary sentence from a topic, reference documents, and the summary generated so far.
WIKICITE contains 486,015 summary-cloze instances collected from Wikipedia and web references.
Wikipedia section headings and article titles are used as high-level topic information.
The ContentSelector combines representations of reference sentences with topic and context representations through attention.
The abstractive system first reduces the reference material extractively and then generates the cloze.
The preceding summary is used to initialize the abstractive decoder and also influences its coverage mechanism.
Human-written clozes were closer to the gold cloze when writers had access to topic and context.
Removing context from ContentSelector hurt performance more than removing the topic.
The topic did not significantly improve the learned ContentSelector in the reported extractive experiment.
ContentSelector remained far below the oracle extractor.
Adding context improved the abstractive results across tested extraction preprocessing methods.
The authors note that many different clozes can be valid, which makes single-reference automatic evaluation difficult.
